explanation: Scan multiplier bits; add a shifted multiplicand for each set bit. Addition itself repeatedly combines XOR sums and shifted AND carries, using no multiplication operator.
timeComplexity: O(w²) carry/shift operation steps as an upper bound: up to w multiplier positions each perform up to w carry steps. Python integer operations also have width-dependent cost.
spaceComplexity: O(w) recursive carry frames, each holding growing integers; O(w²) bits is a conservative peak bound when w bounds the intermediate bit width.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/primitive_multiply.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: At each outer iteration, the accumulated product plus the unprocessed multiplicand times the shifted multiplier equals the original product. A set low bit contributes the shifted multiplier, after which shifting advances to the next bit. The Add helper preserves a+b because XOR holds carry-free sums and shifted AND holds pending carries; no arithmetic addition or multiplication is needed.
walkthrough: For x=13 (binary 1101) and y=6, the set bits select 6,24 and 48. The carry-propagating helper combines those contributions into 78. The shifted contribution 12 is skipped because bit 1 of x is zero.
edgeCases: Long results are assembled without converting bits to strings.
Input/result values must satisfy the displayed long contract.
